exists: infrastructure.json schema_version 1.0.0, reference_date 1914-01-01; static snapshot (no dynamic state).

90 regions in regional_infrastructure, each with region_id, name_fr, sovereign_1914, strategic_site_ids, major_port_ids, fortification_ids, connected_railway_axis_ids, has_major_port, has_fortification, source_refs.

129 railway axes as GeoJSON LineString features in railways.features; network_class: 117 'main' (is_major_axis=true) and 12 'secondary'; each has id, name_fr, from/to_region_id, from/to_site_id, coordinates, source_refs.
84 major ports listed in major_port_ids (city IDs pointing to cities.json) and repeated per region; 59 regions flagged has_major_port=true.

65 fortifications as GeoJSON features with id, name_fr, name_key, region_id, sovereign_1914, historical_type (many types, e.g. 17 coastal_naval_fortress), reference_year, source_refs; 59 regions flagged has_fortification=true.
175 distinct strategic_site_ids (city IDs) referenced across regions; 22 distinct sovereign_1914 values.

237 region-level railway-axis references across regions (129 unique axes); 83 of 90 regions reference at least one axis; 7 regions have none (e.g. region_039, region_051, region_075, region_076, region_083, region_086, region_090).

world_map.gd loads data/game/world_map.json (format 'gs1914.world_map') into immutable WorldMap: regions, cities, region_ids (sorted), neighbors (land|strait), maritime_links (region -> zone), maritime_zones, rail_links keyed by sorted 'a|b' region pairs, source_sha256.
world_map.gd exposes has_rail_link(a,b), neighbor_ids(rid, allow_straits), connection_kind(a,b), shortest_path(a,b, passable, allow_straits) (unweighted, counts regions) and label_point(rid).

logistics_system.gd implements territorial continuity: friendly() (owner==nation or active 'alliance' treaty), accessible_regions() BFS from capital over friendly regions via land+straits, update_supply() sets formation 'supplied' and logs cut-off events, summary() returns controlled / accessible / cut_off.
logistics_system.gd explicitly documents the distinction: possede = national stocks (ECO-01 to source), accessible = computed continuity, livre = transport capacities OPEN/null.
partial: connected_railway_axis_ids / WorldMap.rail_links are existence-only: a list of axis IDs and a boolean 'a|b' key. No capacity, gauge, track count, travel time, cost, owner/controller or operational state; has_rail_link() only tests key presence.

railways.features carry name/network_class/is_major_axis/endpoints/geometry but no throughput, ownership, condition, double-track, electrification or transit time; no link from a rail feature to a port node.
major_port_ids is a flat ID list only: no throughput/berths/draft, no naval vs commercial classification, no owner/operator, no state, no rail or road connection, no maritime zone linkage.
fortifications record presence, type and 1914 sovereign but no garrison, condition or estate; infrastructure, not a transport asset.
maritime_links/maritime_zones give region->zone membership but no sea-lane edges, no capacity, no ownership, no navigability/blockade state.

logistics 'supplied' is derived from territorial adjacency only, not from rail/port capacity; summary()['delivered'] is hardcoded null with delivered_status 'OUVERT : capacites de transport non definies'.
shortest_path() is unweighted (number of regions); it cannot represent distance, time, capacity bottlenecks or modal cost.
supply has no consequence: update_supply() computes and displays state only; penalties undefined (dossier 7.2).
Rail network is documented as fragmented into 17 connected components (logistics_system.gd header, docs/map/decisions/THEMATIC_LAYERS.md); existence of a link does not guarantee rail connectivity.
Note in infrastructure.json states inter-batch railway connections (MAJ-002) remain to be sourced.
missing: Capacity/throughput attributes on every transport edge (tons/day, trains/day, ships/day, berths, draft).
Ownership/controller and dynamic operational state (operational / damaged / destroyed / blocked) for rail links, ports, sea lanes and routes.
Route objects: no modeled itinerary with ordered nodes/links, mode sequence, total cost/time and bottleneck capacity; no multi-modal (rail+road+sea) routing.
Road network data entirely absent although logistics_system.gd mentions 'routes'.
Port-to-rail and port-to-sea-lane connectivity with capacities; maritime_zones have no edges or capacities.
Weighted pathfinding: shortest_path() ignores distance/time/capacity, so a 'delivered' calculation cannot be built on it.
National stock data ('possede', ECO-01) required as supply source.
Inter-batch rail connections (MAJ-002) still unsourced; 17 disconnected rail components not reconciled.
Static-only data: no timestamp/turn-varying state for infrastructure degradation or capture.
Named company/operator attribution for the 129 rail axes (only historical name_fr and source_refs today).

rail_link.id: string, stable; reuse existing railways.features id and infrastructure connected_railway_axis_ids (e.g. 'rail_fr_paris_lille')
rail_link.pair_key: string 'a|b' with a<b region IDs, to stay compatible with WorldMap.rail_links / has_rail_link()

port.id: string, reuse existing major_port_ids city ID (e.g. 'city_london')
port.rail_link_ids: array of rail_link ids connecting to this port

route.nodes: ordered array of region/city/port node IDs

notes: Audit of the three authorized files only. Confirmed counts: 90 regions, 129 railway axes (117 main / 12 secondary), 84 major ports, 65 fortifications, 59 regions with a port, 59 with a fortification; also 175 distinct strategic sites and 22 sovereigns. The suggested 184 and 20 could NOT be confirmed in these three files (184 is absent; 20 appears only as region_020-style IDs, and no count of 20 entities exists) -- they likely refer to cities.json / nation count in other data and are out of scope here. Transport data is topological only: existence of axes, ports and rail adjacency, plus unweighted continuity BFS; capacity, ownership, dynamic state and any 'delivered' computation are explicitly open/null. Recommended schemas add capacity, ownership/controller, state and route objects while preserving existing IDs and the 'a|b' rail key.
